html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. HR: human resources; AI: artificial intelligence; GDPR: General Data Protection Regulation; HIPAA: Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act

  • Which uses of Claude are appropriate, need extra controls, or are not allowed
  • How to classify data and decide what may go into Claude
  • How to protect privacy: minimize, anonymize, use approved tools and settings
  • What regulation means for everyday use

2Appropriate and Inappropriate Use Cases

Running case

Cedarbrook's Three Requests

  • Marketing wants Claude to draft a spring campaign
  • HR wants Claude to rank candidates and send rejections
  • Finance wants Claude to check a file of raw payment-card details for errors
  • The first is fine; the second needs a person to decide; the third should not happen as asked

Zone Examples What to do
Appropriate Drafting, summarizing public or non-sensitive material, brainstorming, formatting, learning, planning Use normally; still check accuracy
Allowed with controls High-risk areas: legal, medical, financial, credit, insurance, housing, employment, education, public benefits; any work with personal or confidential data Qualified human reviews before delivery or action; tell affected people AI was involved; follow policy; minimize data
Not allowed Anything that breaks the law or Anthropic's Usage Policy: fraud, phishing, harassment, disinformation, fake reviews, unauthorized access, weapons, sexually explicit content, surveillance or tracking people without consent, misuse of others' private data Do not do it; report concerns to your policy owner
  • The Usage Policy also covers deception: artificial activity (sockpuppets, astroturfing, fake reviews), impersonation, and false election or medical claims.
  • High-risk decisions about people need a human who can change the result; Claude's output is advice, not the decision.
  • Consumer-facing chatbots must make clear that the user is dealing with AI.
  • Ask: Is the purpose lawful and ethical? Is the data allowed? What if the output is wrong? Who is accountable?
Exam tip

Sort scenarios into the three zones. Legal, medical, hiring, credit and similar decisions are allowed only with qualified human review and disclosure; deception and unauthorized access are not allowed.

3Data Sensitivity

Class Examples Rule of thumb
Public Published catalog, press releases Fine to use
Internal Draft plans, internal procedures, non-sensitive metrics Use with approved tools and accounts per policy
Confidential Contracts, unreleased products, pricing strategy, source code, trade secrets Only if policy permits and the tool and plan are approved; limit scope
Regulated / sensitive Personal data (PII): names with account numbers, addresses, IDs; health data (PHI); payment card data; financial account numbers; children's data; credentials and passwords Do not paste unless policy and the contract explicitly allow it; otherwise remove or anonymize

Principles

  • Data minimization: share only what the task needs.
  • Anonymize or redact identifiers before upload (replace names with IDs like "Customer 17"; remove account numbers, emails, phone numbers).
  • Never put passwords, keys or secrets in prompts, Projects, skills or artifacts.
  • Follow your organization's policy first. Product settings do not override company rules.
  • Think about third parties: customer, patient and colleague data belongs to people who did not consent to your use.
Exam tip

When a scenario shows personal data and a restrictive policy, the best answer is to remove or anonymize the identifiers (or use an approved, covered setup) before using Claude. "Tell Claude not to keep it" or "it's only internal" does not satisfy the policy.

4Privacy Controls in the Product

Topic What to know
Model training (consumer plans) On Free, Pro and Max, chats may be used to improve models if you allow it (a Model Improvement setting under privacy settings), or if flagged for safety review; incognito chats are never used. Check the setting yourself [Verify live]
Commercial plans Team, Enterprise and the API are governed by commercial terms; Anthropic does not train on customer content from these by default. A data processing addendum and, for health data, a business associate agreement for eligible commercial customers are separate contracts
Work vs personal accounts Use the company-approved account for work data; do not use a personal account for company information
Incognito chat Not saved to history or memory; but it is still subject to retention for safety (30 days) and to company policy
Memory Sensitive topics are off by default; some items are never saved; review and delete memory; Team and Enterprise owners cannot read individual memories
Shared chats Sharing creates a link anyone can open; attached files and raw tool data are not included; unshare in Settings; on Team and Enterprise sharing stays inside the organization
Artifacts Private by default; check whether shared storage is used before entering sensitive information; do not run untrusted artifacts
Connectors Claude sees only what you can access; keep connected sources narrow; approvals before sending or sharing; connector data is not used for training
Files and code execution Instructions hidden in untrusted files or sites (prompt injection) could try to make Claude leak conversation data; monitor actions; use files from trusted sources
Web search and fetch Claude may use your approximate location; it reads public pages; do not paste confidential text into a search
Feedback Thumbs up or down can store the whole conversation for review and analysis (up to five years, delinked from your ID)

5Regulation and Everyday Use

  • Regulations (for example GDPR and similar privacy laws, HIPAA for health data, rules for payment card data, sector rules, AI laws) apply to how data about people is processed, no matter which tool you use.
  • The associate's job is not to interpret law but to recognize when regulated data or a high-risk decision is involved, follow the organization's policy, and ask Legal, Privacy or Security when unsure.
  • Be aware of data residency, retention and contract terms for the account you use; these differ between consumer and commercial plans and across cloud options.
  • AI-generated content marking: Claude outputs may carry invisible watermarks or content credentials; a mark is a signal, not proof, and a missing mark proves nothing.
  • Keep a record of how AI was used on important work.

Exam tip

Sort every scenario into appropriate, allowed with controls, or not allowed, then check the data class before you share anything.

6Exam Q&A

S1A store manager wants Claude to find the busiest delivery hours from an export of orders that lists each customer's full name, home address and phone number. Company policy restricts personal data in AI tools. What is the best action?

  • AGive up on the analysis
  • BStrip or replace the personal columns with order numbers, then analyze the reduced data
  • CUpload the export as it is because the findings stay inside the company
  • DUpload the export and add a line asking Claude to forget it afterward
Show the answer

Answer: B. Removing the identifiers keeps the analysis possible and satisfies the policy; the other options either breach it or abandon the task unnecessarily.

S2Which request should be refused or stopped?

  • ADrafting a campaign plan for the spring catalog with the marketing team
  • BBrainstorming product names
  • CSummarizing a public report for colleagues who need the key figures quickly
  • DWriting fake five-star reviews under invented customer names
Show the answer

Answer: D. Fake reviews are deceptive artificial activity and violate the Usage Policy.

S3HR wants Claude to rank applicants and automatically reject the bottom half. What is the best response?

  • AAllow it, because ranking candidates is only a routine task that Claude does faster and more fairly than any person
  • BHide AI use from applicants
  • CLet Claude decide faster
  • DUse Claude only to support review, keep a qualified person deciding, and tell applicants AI was involved
Show the answer

Answer: D. Employment is a high-risk area that needs a human decision-maker and disclosure.

S4A consultant uses a personal free account to analyze a client's confidential contract. What is the main concern?

  • AFree accounts are far too fast, which makes it impossible for anyone to review the contract carefully
  • BA personal account may lack the commercial terms and controls that client data requires
  • CThe contract is too short
  • DContracts cannot be summarized
Show the answer

Answer: B. Use the approved account and follow policy for confidential data.

S5An employee puts a customer's home address into an incognito chat, thinking that makes it private. What is true?

  • AIncognito deletes the data instantly
  • BIncognito sends the data to the customer
  • CIncognito removes all policy obligations
  • DIncognito keeps the chat out of history and memory, but company policy and retention rules still apply
Show the answer

Answer: D. Incognito is not an exemption from policy; chats are still retained for safety for a period.

S6Which TWO are good privacy habits when using Claude at work? Select TWO.

  • AAssume everything is private
  • BRedact or anonymize personal identifiers
  • CShare only the data the task needs
  • DUse a personal account for client work
  • EPaste passwords so Claude can log in
Show the answer

Answer: B, C. Sharing only the data a task needs and redacting personal identifiers are the core privacy practices for everyday work with Claude.

S7What does sharing a chat by link do?

  • ADeletes the chat
  • BEmails it to Anthropic
  • CCreates a snapshot that anyone with the link can view, so avoid sharing sensitive content
  • DKeeps the chat private to you, because only people you invite by name can ever open the link
Show the answer

Answer: C. Shared chats are viewable by anyone with the link (on commercial plans, sharing stays within the organization).

S8A document from an unknown website contains hidden text telling Claude to send the conversation to a web address. What is this?

  • AA billing message
  • BA prompt injection attempt: use trusted sources and stop Claude if it acts unexpectedly
  • CA helpful feature that lets documents tell Claude what to do with the rest of the conversation
  • DA formatting error
Show the answer

Answer: B. Untrusted files can contain instructions that try to misuse Claude.

S9Which statement about regulated data is best?

  • AUsers should recognize regulated data and high-risk decisions, follow policy, and ask Legal or Privacy when unsure
  • BProduct settings override company policy
  • CRegulations do not apply to AI tools
  • DInterpreting the law is the job of every single user, who must decide alone whether a given rule applies to the task
Show the answer

Answer: A. Users are not expected to interpret law; they recognize regulated data and high-risk decisions, follow policy and ask Legal or Privacy.

S10Which data class can usually be used freely in Claude?

  • ACustomer payment card numbers
  • BA published product catalog
  • CUnreleased pricing strategy
  • DEmployee health records
Show the answer

Answer: B. Public information is low risk; the others need controls or must not be used.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Three zones Appropriate · allowed with controls and human review · not allowed
High-risk areas Legal, medical, financial, credit, insurance, housing, employment, education, public benefits
Not allowed Fraud, fake reviews, harassment, disinformation, unauthorized access, surveillance without consent
Data classes Public · internal · confidential · regulated (PII, PHI, payment, credentials)
Rules Minimize · anonymize or redact · never share secrets · policy first
Not a control "Don't retain this" instruction · incognito alone · "it's internal"
Accounts Company-approved account for work data; commercial terms for business data
Sharing Link = anyone can view; unshare in Settings
Prompt injection Untrusted files and sites can carry instructions; monitor
Regulation Recognize, follow policy, ask Legal, Privacy or Security
